decisions.title: Encore! Encore!
decisions.situation: You bang a spoon on a bowl. It makes a brilliant noise. You would like to check that result another twenty times.

choices.label: Give the full concert
Try a different rhythm
Look inside the bowl

result.title: A short, loud career
result.body: You keep banging until you drop the spoon. You look very pleased with yourself.

journal.text: I discovered how much noise a spoon and a bowl could make.

decisions.title: Your name is No
decisions.situation: You decide Hugo is called “No”, because they say it so often. You introduce them to a visitor as No. No looks tired.

choices.label: Ask No for a biscuit
Ask whether their middle name is Stop
Give them their old name back

result.title: They answer to it
result.body: Hugo says no. You point out that they have just said their own name. The visitor needs a moment.

journal.text: I named Hugo No, then asked No for a biscuit.

decisions.title: Something in your sock
decisions.situation: You hide an ice cube in your sock. Hugo asks why your foot is leaking. You had not planned for questions.

choices.label: Show Hugo your disappearing treasure
Try the other sock
Ask to put your sock in the freezer

result.title: One wet sock
result.body: You turn the sock out over a bowl. A tiny cube slides out. Hugo supplies a dry sock; you inspect the bowl for the rest of your treasure.

journal.text: I showed Hugo the ice cube I had hidden in my sock.

decisions.title: Heavy traffic
decisions.situation: A caterpillar is crossing a path. It has a lot of feet and very little urgency.

choices.label: Crouch down and watch
Give it plenty of room
Challenge it to a race

result.title: Eventually, the other side
result.body: It reaches the edge and disappears under a leaf. You remain impressed by all the feet.

journal.text: I watched a caterpillar cross a path.

decisions.title: A very short biography
decisions.situation: Leo passes you a homemade book called “People Who Smell Weird”. Your name is on page one. Every other page is blank.

choices.label: Give it a terrible review
Ask why they made it about you
Write their name on every remaining page

result.title: Needs more characters
result.body: You write “repetitive, poorly researched” on the cover. Leo laughs, then admits they could not think of a second chapter.

journal.text: I reviewed Leo’s insulting homemade book as a disappointed critic.

decisions.title: The headteacher is three mice
decisions.situation: Leo wants help with a class newsletter. The headline is “Headteacher Replaced by Three Mice”. Their evidence is a chewed worksheet.

choices.label: Investigate before printing it
Draw a wanted poster for the mice
Leave the rodent conspiracy to them

result.title: One human, several questions
result.body: The headteacher is visibly one person. Leo reluctantly changes the headline to “Worksheet Damaged”. Your reporting improves; circulation probably will not.

journal.text: I helped Leo check a ridiculous newsletter claim.

decisions.title: The staffroom boss fight
decisions.situation: You copied your school map from a video game. Leo wants to know why the staffroom is labelled “FINAL BOSS” and the toilets contain treasure.

choices.label: Replace the monsters with actual rooms
Ask whether the staffroom really is off limits
Insist the treasure is in the toilets

result.title: A less dangerous school
result.body: You redraw the map. The dragon becomes the library. Leo marks the corrected version and circles the one staircase you accidentally kept.

journal.text: I replaced a video-game map with a real map of my school.

decisions.title: Birthday invitation
decisions.situation: Leo invites you to a birthday party at an arcade. The invitation has more glitter than useful information.

choices.label: Ask Hugo for permission
Ask Leo for more details
Politely decline

result.title: Adults need an address
result.body: Hugo checks the time and supervision. Their answer and any plan are recorded below. Nothing is paid just for asking.

journal.text: I asked Hugo for permission to go to Leo’s arcade birthday.

decisions.title: Party day
decisions.situation: Leo’s arcade birthday is here. Hugo agreed to take you. The quoted outing costs 12,50 €, paid by Hugo only if you go.

choices.label: Go with Hugo · 12,50 €
Stay home · no charge

result.title: High score, low dignity
result.body: You and Leo take turns at the machines. Hugo pays the quoted outing cost. Nobody wins enough tickets to retire.

journal.text: I went to Leo’s arcade birthday with Hugo.

decisions.title: You are in verse two
decisions.situation: Leo asks you to help rehearse a song about everyone who has annoyed them. Your name appears in verse two. The rhyme is frankly weak.

choices.label: Suggest a better rhyme for your insult
Ask why you made the track list
Walk out before verse three

result.title: An unwilling co-writer
result.body: You improve the line and rehearse the chorus. Leo laughs, then admits that your original offence was borrowing a pencil.

journal.text: I helped Leo rehearse a song that included an insult about me.

decisions.title: Fun fact about yourself
decisions.situation: You must introduce yourself with one fun fact. The person before you announces they once swallowed a coin. Everyone turns to you expecting escalation.

choices.label: Give your name and disappoint them
Claim you only eat paper money
Recite your entire biography at speed

result.title: No coins were harmed
result.body: You say you like music. A perfectly ordinary fact survives in a room briefly obsessed with swallowing things.

journal.text: I gave a simple introduction after someone set an alarming standard.

decisions.title: Read at 10:42
decisions.situation: Hugo sends “Where are you?” You are somewhere perfectly ordinary, but the fourth message arrives before you finish typing.

choices.label: Reply, then talk about check-ins
Send a spectacularly boring photo
Ignore all four

result.title: A workable arrangement
result.body: You agree on a check-in time. Hugo admits the silence worried them.

journal.text: I agreed on clearer check-ins with Hugo.

decisions.title: A striking resemblance
decisions.situation: A caricaturist at a street fair in Valencia offers you a free sample portrait. A small crowd gathers. The artist turns the drawing around. It is you as an enormous angry thumb.

choices.label: Ask whether they could add a jawline
Ask for a pencil and draw the artist
Cover the portrait and leave

result.title: The formal thumb
result.body: The artist adds a bow tie. You point out that this is not a jawline. A spectator says the resemblance is uncanny. You leave holding a thumb in evening wear.

journal.text: I asked a caricaturist to correct my portrait and received a thumb in a bow tie.

decisions.title: Money is falling from the sky
decisions.situation: A gust sends banknotes across a square in Valencia. You grab one before spotting a film crew and the words FOR FILM USE across the back.

choices.label: Help return the prop notes
Pose briefly like a terrible billionaire
Insist the prop note is now yours

result.title: An honest counterfeit cleanup
result.body: You collect paper money worth precisely nothing. A crew member thanks you while chasing a very wealthy-looking pigeon.

journal.text: I helped a film crew recover wind-blown prop money in Valencia.

decisions.title: The accidental millionaire
decisions.situation: At a charity auction, someone mistakes you for a wealthy donor. The auctioneer hands you the microphone beside a photograph of an elderly donkey. “How much will you give?” The room goes quiet.

choices.label: Admit your wealth has been exaggerated
Donate €240.13 to the donkey charity
Claim you are the donkey’s lawyer

result.title: A donkey-sized misunderstanding
result.body: You explain that you were looking for the toilets. The auctioneer takes back the microphone and points down the corridor. Several people applaud your honesty. One applauds the donkey.

journal.text: I admitted I was not the wealthy donor a charity auction expected.

decisions.title: The naked gardener
decisions.situation: The community garden in Valencia needs volunteers. Its organiser is wearing a novelty apron printed with a naked torso and refuses to explain it.

choices.label: Weed beside the alarming apron
Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

journal.text: I volunteered beside a gardener in an alarming novelty apron in Valencia.

decisions.title: The important businessman
decisions.situation: You sit in the last free café chair. A child wearing an enormous tie tells you it is reserved for an important businessman. The businessman, they explain, is them.

choices.label: Ask what business they are in
Offer them the chair after your drink
Explain that reserving chairs is bad business

result.title: A volatile juice market
result.body: They explain that juice has gone up and crayons are a bad investment. You move to the counter while they hold a meeting with a biscuit.

journal.text: I gave up a café chair after hearing a child’s business plan.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: persistent worry and disrupted sleep. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs €0.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: Any difficult questions?
decisions.situation: At a free talk, a speaker claims nobody has ever disproved their theory. The theory is that pigeons remember your face and discuss you at night.

choices.label: Ask how they interviewed the pigeons
Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work
result.body: They admit they inferred the conversations. You learn the difference between a suspicious bird and actual evidence.

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Drink the tap water
Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: The door does not believe in you
decisions.situation: An automatic shop door refuses to open for you. It opens for a child, a trolley and a blowing receipt. You step forward. Nothing. The cashier points at the sensor and suggests waving.

choices.label: Ask the cashier to let you out
Follow the trolley out
Perform an increasingly furious dance

result.title: Assisted departure
result.body: The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.

journal.text: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

decisions.title: Your murderous past
decisions.situation: A walking-tour guide points straight at you and tells the group you are the ghost of a notorious murderer. You are outside a shop in Valencia, holding a sandwich.

choices.label: Explain that you are alive and eating lunch
Ask what crimes you supposedly committed
Follow the tour without breaking eye contact

result.title: New evidence
result.body: The guide calls your sandwich an unsettling detail. You take a large bite. A tourist asks whether ghosts can eat cheese. The guide moves the group along.

journal.text: I corrected a walking tour that mistook me for a murderer’s ghost in Valencia.

decisions.title: The quiet place has noises
decisions.situation: You sit somewhere quiet and immediately notice a clock, a distant door and somebody clearing their throat. Apparently quiet did not mean perfectly silent.

choices.label: Let the ordinary sounds be there
Choose one steady sound to notice
Identify every interruption

result.title: Quiet enough is available
result.body: You stop checking each sound for a reason to be irritated. The place becomes restful without becoming silent.

journal.text: I accepted ordinary background sounds in a quiet moment.

decisions.title: The sofa is judging you
decisions.situation: Autoplay follows your programme with a competitive fitness class. A man who appears to have been assembled entirely from elbows challenges you to beat your personal best.

choices.label: Switch to the beginner version and try it
Invent a chair-based version
Keep up with him at full speed

result.title: An achievable number of elbows
result.body: You complete the gentler routine. The instructor says anyone can do it, then folds himself into a shape you decline to investigate.

journal.text: I followed a beginner workout after a fitness video appeared on autoplay.

decisions.title: The missing letter
decisions.situation: A poster for a free public cookery class has dropped the L from “public”. The organiser cannot work out why people keep arriving with suspicious questions.

choices.label: Point out the missing letter quietly
Leave the organiser to discover it
Read the heading aloud to the queue

result.title: A little tape saves the afternoon
result.body: The organiser repairs the heading and looks at the queue with fresh concern. The class returns to soup.

journal.text: I pointed out an embarrassing typo on a cookery-class poster.

decisions.title: A shortcut through the execution

choices.label: Take the long route
Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

decisions.title: Doing nothing, attendance required

choices.label: Cancel it and protect your hour
Host exactly five minutes of nothing
Send an agenda for competitive relaxing

result.title: A successful cancellation
result.body: You explain that it was private. Someone replies that they were really looking forward to nothing. You enjoy it without them.

journal.text: I cancelled accidental invitations to my free hour.

decisions.title: Not the tabletop version
decisions.situation: At a craft workshop, you pull the tab on a kit labelled “decorative boat”. A full-size inflatable canoe starts filling the room. The tiny instruction sheet says to inflate outdoors.

choices.label: Deflate it before it reaches the doorway
Climb in and ask for paddles
Insist the picture on the box was misleading

result.title: A long public fart
result.body: You open the valve. The canoe collapses over eight uninterrupted seconds of rude noise. The instructor waits until everyone has stopped laughing to explain the warning.

journal.text: I deflated a full-size canoe during a crowded craft workshop.

decisions.title: Nothing to worry about

choices.label: Ask what the label means
Step back and let them stop it
Ask whether smoke costs extra

result.title: A useful admission
result.body: The volunteer stops and explains the failed mechanism. You learn more from the mistake than from the planned demonstration.

journal.text: I asked about a warning label during a failed toy-repair demonstration.

decisions.title: A minute without filling it

choices.label: Look around for a minute
Let your attention rest
Check the same screen again

result.title: The world supplies a few details
result.body: You notice a small sign and an interesting pattern of light. The wait becomes a moment rather than a gap to erase.

journal.text: I spent a short wait noticing what was around me.

Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

decisions.title: Older than bread
decisions.situation: A birthday cake for you arrives with an extra zero among the candles. Someone asks whether you knew the person who invented bread.

choices.label: Ask for the extra candles to be removed
Keep the cake and accept your ancient status
Deliver a speech about surviving the last ice age

result.title: A breakthrough in reverse ageing
result.body: They remove the extra candles, then stand back as though they have made you younger. You thank the bakery for its medical breakthrough.

journal.text: I corrected an extra zero on my birthday cake.

decisions.title: Happy statistical decline
decisions.situation: For your birthday, someone sends a list of famous people who had achieved more by your age. They finish with “Hope this inspires you!”

choices.label: Celebrate without the comparison chart
Choose one goal that is actually yours
Read every biography before bed

result.title: Cake remains an achievement
result.body: You put the list aside. Your day improves immediately when it stops competing with a dead inventor.

journal.text: I ignored an unhelpful achievement list on my birthday.

decisions.title: A complaint from your younger self
decisions.situation: You find a note from your younger self: By fifty-five, we will be independently wealthy and know how to fold a fitted sheet. The handwriting is extremely confident.

choices.label: Write back about the sheet
List what you did achieve
Send your younger self a furious reply

result.title: The corners remain hostile
result.body: You report that the elastic corners remain a problem. You omit finances; you are not being interrogated by a child with a felt-tip pen.

journal.text: I answered an old note about being wealthy and folding fitted sheets.

decisions.title: The naked gardener
decisions.situation: The community garden in Valencia needs volunteers. Its organiser is wearing a novelty apron printed with a naked torso and refuses to explain it.

choices.label: Weed beside the alarming apron
Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

journal.text: I volunteered beside a gardener in an alarming novelty apron in Valencia.

decisions.title: You are almost in the picture
decisions.situation: An old photograph catches you at the edge of the frame, apparently concentrating on something outside it. You can no longer remember what seemed so important.

choices.label: Enjoy the unfinished little mystery
Write down what you do remember
Build a grand explanation around the pose

result.title: A life outside the frame
result.body: You let the unknown detail remain unknown. The photograph still holds an ordinary moment worth keeping.

journal.text: I enjoyed an old photograph without solving every detail.

decisions.title: You must make the most of it
decisions.situation: You feel better rested than usual and immediately begin planning enough tasks to use every available bit of energy.

choices.label: Choose a few priorities and leave room
Enjoy feeling well without a quota
Fill every bit of the day

result.title: A useful day with an ending
result.body: You use some energy without treating all of it as a resource that must be exhausted.

journal.text: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

decisions.title: Beginners’ self-defence
decisions.situation: At a free beginner lesson, the instructor asks you to demonstrate a firm “No!” You give one so convincing that a passer-by apologises and leaves.

choices.label: Practise the rest of the lesson
Watch the demonstrations first
Use your new “No!” on the whole lesson

result.title: A useful loud afternoon
result.body: You learn the basics and repeat the shout. The corridor remains unusually clear for the rest of the lesson.

journal.text: I practised the basics at a free self-defence lesson.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: unusual thirst and persistent fatigue. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs €0.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: The sofa is judging you
decisions.situation: Autoplay follows your programme with a competitive fitness class. A man who appears to have been assembled entirely from elbows challenges you to beat your personal best.

choices.label: Switch to the beginner version and try it
Invent a chair-based version
Keep up with him at full speed

result.title: An achievable number of elbows
result.body: You complete the gentler routine. The instructor says anyone can do it, then folds himself into a shape you decline to investigate.
